_about: Hand-maintained part of the CMA data map. Every table in schema cma has one entry under a group; every computed view in cma_read (not a table view, not dq_*) has one entry under derived. flows are the paths the page draws: per source its box (src, a data-id in template.html, null when it has none), its ways in (ways, data-ids) and the groups it fills (doms, group keys); every group is in at least one flow. Columns come from schema.json, never from here. Edit, then run node tools/datamap/build.mjs.

tables.name: crm_record
tables.what: Deals and tickets: pipeline, stage, owner, market, closed; the reason's option value from the mapped dropdown property, never free text (0008zb)
tables.how: HubSpot webhook, read back within seconds; nightly reconcile 02:30

tables.name: crm_record_stage
tables.what: A deal's latest entry into and exit from each pipeline stage that reads its times: pipeline, stage, entered, exited (0008za)
tables.how: HubSpot's own stage history (the calculated hs_v2_date_entered and hs_v2_date_exited properties of each stage that reads times), read with the deal on the webhook's read-back within seconds, else by the next sweep; nightly reconcile 02:30; backfill --again

tables.name: crm_contact
tables.what: Thin contact: country with the slot it came from, language, currency, store, the customer segment (a mapped property's value, 1 to 100 characters, no @; none once the contact is deleted or forgotten; 0008zt), and when it was created in the source (0008u)
tables.how: Read when a deal, ticket, email or inbox thread points to it (the email poll every minute, once, after the email or thread), every country slot and created-time slot (the object's createdAt and the configured properties, the earliest kept) and, since 0008zt, the mapped segment property (its value kept in the segment column, never in raw; no change to the HubSpot scopes or webhooks); re-read every 10 min in its first hour; nightly reconcile; since 0008zn also a contact a store customer is linked to, taken in by the sweep's second read (the links of the last hour, newest first, within ten minutes of the link), by the nightly reconcile's 26-hour look-back for the links the sweep did not reach and by ingest-backfill --object linked_contact

tables.name: crm_contact_ref
tables.what: A contact's ids in other systems, such as its Shopify id
tables.how: With every contact read

tables.name: crm_call
tables.what: Call engagements logged on the contact
tables.how: HubSpot webhook; nightly reconcile

tables.name: crm_association
tables.what: Links between CRM objects, such as deal to contact
tables.how: With every read-back, and the email poll's engagements (email to contact, deal, ticket)

tables.name: form_submission
tables.what: Form submissions: form, page, UTM, contact id only, and the answers to the form's kept choice fields (option values only)
tables.how: Form poll: every counted form every minute, every polled-only form every forms_poll_interval_minutes (default 5, staggered by form; CMA-069), counted in Intake or not (addition 0008p); the nightly reconcile reads every polled form's submissions of the last 26 hours and writes those the poll missed; the form backfill fills a stored submission's empty answers once

tables.name: crm_task
tables.what: Tasks: owner, status, type, priority, due and completed times, the contact, deal and ticket by id; never body or subject
tables.how: HubSpot webhook (task creation, deletion, status, due, owner, completion, type, priority, associations), read back within seconds; nightly reconcile 02:30; backfill by hand (since 0008n)

tables.name: connection_task_status
tables.what: Task statuses seen per connection, with is_done as configuration
tables.how: Seeded by the first task read of each status ref; is_done and the label set on Configuration, Sources

tables.name: connection_task_type
tables.what: Task types seen per connection, with is_callback and is_counted as configuration
tables.how: Seeded by the first task read of each type ref; is_callback and is_counted set on Configuration, Sources

tables.name: email_message
tables.what: Emails, metadata only: CRM email engagements and inbox messages kept apart; direction, status, time, actor kind, the agent's owner id, category, the mailbox (channel account) a message went through, an engagement's origin code (inbox copies and automations told apart by the connection's settings)
tables.how: Email poll every minute (engagements modified since its cursor, with the origin property the connection names; inbox messages of changed threads, with their mailbox), the nightly reconcile (last 26 hours) and the backfill; only when the connection's email_poll is on

tables.name: email_thread
tables.what: Inbox conversations: inbox, channel, the mailbox it came in through, open or closed, the current agent, contact and ticket ids, spam
tables.how: Email poll every minute (threads whose latest message is newer than its cursor; the open check every email_open_check_minutes, default 15; CMA-069), the nightly reconcile (last 26 hours) with the trash check, the backfill; only when the connection's email_poll is on

tables.name: email_thread_event
tables.what: Assignments, closes, reopens and inbox moves of conversations: actor kind and owner ids only
tables.how: Email poll every minute (with the messages of changed threads), the nightly reconcile and the backfill; only when the connection's email_poll is on

tables.name: telephony_call
tables.what: Calls: direction, start, answer, end, talk time, missed reason, line, user
tables.how: Aircall webhook per call event, call read back within seconds; nightly check; backfill by hand

tables.name: telephony_call_tag
tables.what: Tags on each call
tables.how: With the call read

tables.name: telephony_number
tables.what: Lines, their market and whether they count
tables.how: Catalog at most hourly; counting set on Configuration

tables.name: telephony_tag
tables.what: The tag catalog, whether a tag counts and what it means (not reached, incorrect data, call type, courtesy attempt, courtesy completed positive, neutral or negative; 0008zc, incorrect data 0008zd)
tables.how: Catalog at most hourly; counting and meaning set on Configuration, Sources, ingest never writes the meaning

tables.name: telephony_missed_reason
tables.what: Missed-reason labels, service level and callback switches
tables.how: Seed, then Configuration → Sources

tables.name: call_link
tables.what: Aircall call matched to its HubSpot call
tables.how: Sweep every minute, over the last 2 hours

tables.name: commerce_store
tables.what: One row per Shopify store: market, currency, zone
tables.how: Set per store at rollout

tables.name: commerce_customer
tables.what: Customer: state, order count, spend, matched CRM contact
tables.how: Shopify webhook, read back within seconds; nightly check; backfill per store

tables.name: commerce_order
tables.what: Order: amounts, status, kind (first, repeat, renewal), landing page, UTM
tables.how: Shopify webhook, read back within seconds; nightly check; backfill per store

tables.name: commerce_order_line
tables.what: Order lines: SKU, quantity, price
tables.how: With the order read

tables.name: review_channel
tables.what: A review platform's channels per connection: name and locale from the platform, the market each serves and whether its reviews count (configuration); a channel gone from the platform's list is marked, never deleted (0008ze)
tables.how: Reviews poll hourly (the channel list first, again with the nightly reconcile and the backfill); a new channel lands without a market and not counted; market and counted set on Configuration, Sources, which ingest never overwrites

tables.name: review
tables.what: Reviews, metadata only: channel, type, state, published, rating 1 to 5, submitted and updated times, reply, invite event type, transaction reference, and the link to an order or a CRM contact by id; never the reviewer's name, email or phone, nor a title or text (0008ze); the transaction reference holds an order reference only, never an @ (check review_reference_no_at, 0008zf)
tables.how: Reviews poll hourly (each channel's reviews after its cursor less two hours), nightly reconcile (the last reviews_reconcile_days, default 30), backfill by hand; polling only, the platform sends no webhook; the reviewer's email is used in memory to find the CRM contact, then dropped

tables.name: device
tables.what: The asset register's devices per connection, mirrored read-only: record id, serial, model, market and device status from the catalogs (null when unmapped), warehouse, customer, subscription and order references, shipment, stock, warranty and end-of-life dates, the loan it secures (pledge_ref: the register's maatje_id as an id, null for none) and its language (a two-letter code through the language aliases, null when unmapped), named ids of other systems (such as NetSuite's), the row as mapped (raw, key allow-list, never an @); missing from the latest full snapshot as source_deleted_at; never a name, email, phone or address (0008zi, 0009j)
tables.how: Airtable API: changed records every 15 minutes, full snapshot nightly (ingest-poll-assets every 5 minutes, each connection on its assets_poll_interval_minutes, default 15; the full snapshot in the nightly reconcile at 03:30), loaded in chunks of assets_load_chunk rows (default 1000) by cma.ingest_load_device_chunk, each chunk its own call and nothing staged, the next chunk half the size (at least 100) after a call slower than a third of the ingest's statement timeout and a chunk the timeout cancels sent again once at half its size, and a full snapshot ends with cma.ingest_mark_devices_missing in slices of assets_load_chunk record ids, each slice its own call (0008zk); the whole table is read, never a view; CSV fallback a person loads in one call with cma.load_device_snapshot; pledge_ref and language come from the register's maatje_id and language fields, mapped on the connection (sent only while mapped) or in the import's map (0009j)

tables.name: device_component
tables.what: A device's components per kind (pads, battery) with serial and recorded expiry; one current row per device and kind, a changed serial an observed replacement (replaced_at) from the first load on (0008zi); a kind the register empties (serial and expiry both empty) closes the current row with no new one, and the same serial held again reopens it, while another serial is a replacement (0008zk)
tables.how: Airtable API: changed records every 15 minutes, full snapshot nightly (with its device, in chunks by cma.ingest_load_device_chunk, 0008zk); CSV fallback (with its device, by the same load)

tables.name: device_import_row
tables.what: The device import's staged rows: a batch key and the export's mapped columns as text, written through the view device_import_staging (the COPY target) and deleted by the load; a value holding an @ is kept as a bare @, the audit log keeps a staged row's keys only; no name, email, phone or address column (0008zi); pledge_ref and language join the mapped columns (0009j)
tables.how: CSV fallback only (0008zk): staged by tools/devices-to-staging.mjs and psql \copy, read, loaded and emptied by cma.load_device_snapshot in one call; the Airtable API read stages nothing, it loads in chunks by cma.ingest_load_device_chunk

tables.name: device_model
tables.what: Device models with name, brand and the labels the register writes for each (aliases) (0008zi)
tables.how: Tenant configuration: seed 02 for Pulse4all Subscriptions, changed in Studio (no configuration screen yet); read by every load of the register, by the API (0008zj) or from its CSV export

tables.name: device_component_kind
tables.what: The kinds of component that come due (pads, battery), with name and sort order; the key device is reserved for a device's end of life (0008zi)
tables.how: Tenant configuration: seed 02 for Pulse4all Subscriptions, changed in Studio (no configuration screen yet); read by every load of the register, by the API (0008zj) or from its CSV export

tables.name: maintenance_rule
tables.what: Per model and component kind: the interval in months from the anchor date (the day a replacement was first seen, else the last shipment, else the first) and the lead days before the due date (0008zi)
tables.how: Tenant configuration: seed 02 for Pulse4all Subscriptions, changed in Studio (no configuration screen yet); read by every load of the register, by the API (0008zj) or from its CSV export

tables.name: device_status
tables.what: Device statuses with the flags in the field, in stock and tracked (forecast), and the labels the register writes for each; reporting reads the flags, never a name (0008zi)
tables.how: Tenant configuration: seed 02 for Pulse4all Subscriptions, changed in Studio (no configuration screen yet); read by every load of the register, by the API (0008zj) or from its CSV export

tables.name: device_language_alias
tables.what: The register's language labels (an option name such as English, matched lower-cased and trimmed) and the two-letter code each maps to; the pledge file writes the code in capitals (0009j)
tables.how: Tenant configuration set in Studio (cma.set_device_language_alias), no seed; read by every load of the register, by the API or from its CSV export

tables.name: pledge_loan
tables.what: The loans the pledge lists cover: the register's loan reference as key, the loan's number, layout (1 or 2), whether it is active, and the parts of the file's tab names (lender_label, area_label, name_suffix). lender_label is personal data (an investor's name): set in Studio only and kept out of the audit log's images (the audit row says lender_label_changed instead) (0009j)
tables.how: Tenant configuration set in Studio (cma.set_pledge_loan), no seed; read by the pledge lists, today's file and each quarter's take

tables.name: pledge_model_value
tables.what: Per model, as the pledge file shows it: the type label, the acquisition value, the depreciation per month and the receipts (0009j)
tables.how: Tenant configuration set in Studio (cma.set_pledge_model_value), no seed; read by the pledge lists, today's file and each quarter's take

tables.name: pledge_snapshot
tables.what: A quarter file's header: its valuation date (unique per tenant), when and by whom it was taken, the counts of loans and devices, the sources' last reads and file_name_prefix (pledges.file_name_prefix frozen at the take, so the file keeps its name); frozen, an update, delete or truncate is refused (0009j)
tables.how: Taken once per quarter by cma.pledge_snapshot_take in the Flash snapshot job (web/jobs/snapshot-flash.mjs, every minute) on the quarter's first day after pledges.snapshot_local_time in the tenant's zone, or by cma.pledge_snapshot_take_current; the application can only read it

tables.name: pledge_snapshot_row
tables.what: A quarter file's rows as the file showed them, with the loan's number, lender label, area label, name suffix and layout copied in at the take, so a later change of the catalog never alters an old file; lender_label here is personal data, kept with the file for its retention (0009j)
tables.how: Filled with its header by cma.pledge_snapshot_take on a quarter's first day (the Flash snapshot job) or by cma.pledge_snapshot_take_current; frozen, no update or delete, and no path to delete a quarter file

tables.name: subscription
tables.what: A store's subscriptions per subscription connection (one per store), mirrored read-only from the subscription app: its id, the store customer's id (joined to commerce_customer of the store whose handle the connection's account id names), the app's status (active, paused, canceled, expired, failed, merged, never-subscribed), current cycle, next billing time, billing interval and count, amount per cycle and currency, the payment instrument's type only (card, paypal, other), created, paused, canceled and updated times, missing from the latest full read as source_deleted_at, a checked raw (fixed keys, never an @); never a name, email, phone, address or payment detail (0008zl)
tables.how: Juo Admin API, polling only (no webhook for a failed renewal): ingest-poll-subscriptions every 5 minutes reads, per connection when due on subscriptions_poll_interval_minutes (default 5), the events since its cursor less five minutes and then every subscription they touched, by id; the nightly reconcile at 03:30 reads every subscription of the store and marks the ones no longer returned missing in slices (cma.ingest_mark_subscriptions_missing), an empty read failing empty_snapshot; backfill --object subscription [--dry-run] by hand; written by cma.ingest_upsert_subscriptions (stale guard on the source's update time)

tables.name: subscription_event
tables.what: The events of a store's subscriptions, append-only, in the CMA's words: renewed, renew_failed, canceled, paused, resumed, reactivated, status_changed; when, the actor's type (and a staff actor's id only), cycle, attempt, error code, a reason only as a code of the adapter's fixed list, the status before and after, a checked raw (Juo's type under raw.type); never a name, message or free-text reason (0008zl)
tables.how: Juo Admin API: ingest-poll-subscriptions every 5 minutes (the events after its cursor less five minutes; an event held already left as it is), backfill --object subscription_event --from <date> [--dry-run] by hand; Juo's other event types are read and not stored; written by cma.ingest_upsert_subscription_events, insert only

tables.name: integration_connection
tables.what: One row per account of a source (portal, Aircall account, store, review platform account, asset register base, a store's subscription app)
tables.how: Configuration → Sources

tables.name: connection_pipeline
tables.what: CRM pipelines, counted or routed; a ticket pipeline's own SLA in business minutes (0008o); a deal pipeline marked as an order pipeline (0008u)
tables.how: Catalog at most hourly; switches (counted, routed, order pipeline) and the SLA on Configuration

tables.name: connection_stage
tables.what: CRM pipeline stages, closed or open; a deal stage's outcome (won, lost or none) and where it came from (0008u); whether its entry and exit times are read (0008za)
tables.how: Catalog at most hourly, the outcome from the stage's probability (1 won, 0 and closed lost) unless a person set it on Configuration, Sources, which the catalog then keeps; read times on for a counted pipeline's stage unless a person switched it on Configuration, Sources

tables.name: connection_call_outcome
tables.what: CRM call outcomes with a connected flag that no figure reads since 0008zc (the outcome decides neither Connected nor Conversation)
tables.how: Catalog at most hourly

tables.name: connection_form
tables.what: CRM forms: polled, counted in Intake, category, market, kept choice fields, market field, lead condition
tables.how: Form catalog hourly; switches on Configuration (Sources; kept fields, market field and lead condition by the runbook)

tables.name: connection_form_field
tables.what: Fields of the CRM's forms: name, kind (dropdown, radio, checkboxes, other) and a choice field's option values
tables.how: With the form catalog, at most hourly; an option a form drops stays as retired

tables.name: form_category
tables.what: Form categories (what a form is for, such as quote or cancellation): code, name, order, active
tables.how: Configuration (Sources); the tenant's own, filled by the runbook

tables.name: connection_field
tables.what: Which source property feeds which CMA field; a contact's country, refs and created time in ordered slots and its customer segment (one slot, field segment; 0008zt); the property's data type as the adapter last read it, which decides whether a reason is stored (0008zb); on an asset register connection the register's fields, each property an Airtable field id (starting fld): a device's staging columns, a component kind's serial and expiry, the named ids, and each field's type as the ingest first read it (0008zj, 0008zk)
tables.how: Configuration (the reason property on Configuration, Sources; a contact's segment property by cma.set_connection_field(<CRM conn>, 'contact', 'segment', '', <property>, 1)); the data type read by the sweep hourly, or at once while unchecked (0008zb); an asset register's fields by cma.set_connection_field in Studio, from a block generated from the Airtable dry run's field list (docs/ingest/airtable-fields.mjs), the type recorded by the ingest's first read through cma.ingest_record_field_types and a later different type failing the read (0008zj, 0008zk)

tables.name: connection_reason
tables.what: The options of a connection's reason property per record type (a deal's lost reason, a ticket's reason): value, label, order, whether a person marked it data quality, active or archived (0008zb)
tables.how: The sweep reads the mapped dropdown property's options from HubSpot hourly, or at once while its type is unchecked; an option gone is archived, never deleted; the data-quality flag is set on Configuration, Sources and kept by every refresh

tables.name: connection_record_kind
tables.what: The rules that give a connection's records a kind: the kind, a pipeline, a category value or both, active or archived (0008zb)
tables.how: Configuration, Sources, on the connection's page

tables.name: writeback_field
tables.what: Fields the CMA may write back to the CRM
tables.how: Configuration

tables.name: connection_inbox
tables.what: Inboxes of the CRM's conversations: counted, market, work type, channel
tables.how: The email poll's inbox catalog hourly (when the connection's email_poll is on); switches on Configuration

tables.name: connection_inbox_channel
tables.what: Channels of the CRM's conversations (email, chat, ...): the CMA channel, counted
tables.how: The email poll's channel catalog hourly (when the connection's email_poll is on); switches on Configuration

tables.name: connection_inbox_account
tables.what: Mailboxes: the channel accounts of the CRM's inboxes (a shared address connected to an inbox); the source's name, or its id when the name holds an address, a label a person sets, counted, market
tables.how: The email poll's catalog hourly with the inboxes (when the connection's email_poll is on); label, counted and market on Configuration, Sources

tables.name: connection_email_rule
tables.what: Email classification rules: words in a sender domain or subject, the category, in order
tables.how: Configuration (the functions of 0008m; the screen comes with B17c)

tables.name: workday
tables.what: One workday per person and date, in one or more sessions
tables.how: Clock in and out in the Workspace, immediately; hourly job closes forgotten days

tables.name: time_event
tables.what: Clock in, status changes, clock out, corrections
tables.how: Every click in the Workspace, immediately; corrections by supervisors

tables.name: roster_week
tables.what: A team's roster week and its version
tables.how: Roster screen

tables.name: roster_entry
tables.what: Planned shifts and absences
tables.how: Roster screen

tables.name: roster_publication
tables.what: Each published version of a week
tables.how: Publish on the Roster screen

tables.name: import_batch
tables.what: The import batch steam-2026
tables.how: One-off, 12 October 2026

tables.name: import_day
tables.what: Imported days per person
tables.how: One-off

tables.name: import_person_map
tables.what: Old system's person id to CMA person
tables.how: One-off

tables.name: import_session
tables.what: Raw login sessions from the export (2 January to 9 October 2026)
tables.how: One-off

tables.name: legacy_call_batch
tables.what: One imported file of a former telephony system's legacy call outcomes: the source system, the CRM connection it was matched against, the file's SHA-256 (one live batch per file), the cutover date, row counts per match method, times and the withdrawal; no personal data (0008zg)
tables.how: Legacy import (one-off job), on demand: the job ingest-import-legacy-calls started by hand on one export file in a private bucket; the same file again reuses its batch; an admin withdraws a batch once

tables.name: legacy_call_outcome
tables.what: Legacy call outcomes of a former telephony system, one row per imported row: the date, the tag meaning, the former system's tag text, the CRM contact matched (by id) or none, and the match method (email and phone, email, phone, customer id, none, conflict or forgotten); never an email, phone number, name or customer id (0008zg)
tables.how: Legacy import (one-off job), on demand: ingest-import-legacy-calls matches each row of the file to at most one HubSpot contact in memory and writes it; a rerun fills a contact only where none is set and never refills a forgotten row; with the job option --unmatched skip (Pulse4all's choice) only rows matched to exactly one contact are written, none and conflict rows are not stored; the CRM's privacy deletion of a contact sets forgotten

tables.name: app_user
tables.what: People and system users
tables.how: People screen, invitations

tables.name: app_user_external_id
tables.what: A person's HubSpot owner id and Aircall user id
tables.how: People screen

tables.name: app_role
tables.what: Roles per tenant
tables.how: Seed, Configuration

tables.what: Permission catalog
tables.how: Defined by migrations

tables.how: Seed, Configuration

tables.what: A person's role, optionally scoped
tables.how: People screen

tables.how: People screen

tables.how: Teams screen

tables.what: Team membership over time
tables.how: Teams screen

tables.how: Configuration

tables.how: Messages screen, or a rule when a lead is assigned or a published review of a counted channel comes in at or below a review rule's highest rating (the reviews poll, 0008ze); Delete on Messages withdraws one (messages.withdraw)

tables.name: message_delivery

tables.how: As the person opens the message

tables.name: message_rule

tables.how: Configuration → alert rules

tables.what: Business lines (Subscriptions, Invest)
tables.how: Seed

tables.what: Settings per tenant
tables.how: Configuration

tables.what: Settings catalog with defaults
tables.how: Defined by migrations

tables.how: Configuration; the contact-center flag is set by seed 02 or in Studio, no screen writes it

tables.how: Each migration

tables.how: Configuration: the customer's seed (02) and cma.set_journey; never deleted, archived hides one

tables.name: record_kind
tables.what: The tenant's kinds of CRM records the reports count, such as a cancellation request: key, label, record type, order, active or archived (0008zb)
tables.how: Configuration, Sources; none seeded

tables.name: follow_up_snapshot
tables.what: Per tenant: when the follow-up figures were last computed and how long it took, the eight counts and the figures per person (ids and counts, no names)
tables.how: Replaced by the refresh job cma-refresh-follow-up (cma.refresh_follow_up, since 0008s) when something the figures read changed, in office hours every minute; on a minute that found nothing changed (since 0009o) only computed_at is set to now, the figures and duration_ms stay; computed once on demand when a tenant has none

tables.name: follow_up_item
tables.what: Every open lead, ticket and task of the latest refresh: kind, order, market, owner as a person, state, and the row's fields as JSON (ids, codes and times; never a task's text)
tables.how: Written with the snapshot from cma.open_leads_of, open_tickets_of and open_tasks_of (since 0008s); since 0009o only the items that changed are deleted and inserted, the others stay, and nothing is written on a minute that found nothing changed; derived, no audit trigger

tables.name: follow_up_marker
tables.what: Per tenant, what the follow-up job checks before computing again: when the figures were last computed, up to when the audit log of their input tables was read, the first instant a figure moves with the clock alone and how many migrations were held then (0009o)
tables.how: Written by cma.refresh_follow_up_of at each computation and by cma.refresh_follow_up when it confirms nothing changed (setting follow_up.recompute_minutes, 60 by default, is the longest it goes without computing); derived, no audit trigger

tables.name: data_quality_snapshot
tables.what: When one tenant's stored data-quality result was computed (Refreshed at), how long it took and how many findings it holds (0008zr)
tables.how: Rewritten by the job cma-refresh-data-quality every minute when the result is older than data_quality.refresh_minutes (5 by default), and once on demand by a read that finds none; after a failed computation the next attempt waits data_quality.refresh_minutes (since 0009o), not one minute; not audited

tables.name: data_quality_finding
tables.what: The findings of the latest data-quality refresh: the check, the record's connection, type and id, the value the check reports, the market and where it is fixed; ids and codes only (0008zr)
tables.how: Rewritten with the snapshot by cma-refresh-data-quality (cma.flash_findings_compute_of, every check of cma.data_quality_of once); read by Reports → Data quality, Flash's data-quality overview and list, the snapshot take and the watch; after a failed computation the next attempt waits data_quality.refresh_minutes (since 0009o); not audited

tables.name: flash_snapshot_run
tables.what: Per tenant and business date one row per Flash take: when the date was due (due_at), started, finished, status succeeded, failed (with the error's code) or missed (a date that stopped being the latest due one without a succeeded take: no figures), late (the take started more than an hour after it was due), the rows stored per overview and at a month end the ids per kind, the sources' state, the Flash settings followed, the dates missed before it and the watch's error code (watch_error; the snapshot is kept) (0008zn). Written by the take only; the application reads
tables.how: Written by the take only (cma.flash_snapshot_take, SECURITY DEFINER; the application reads and holds no insert, update or delete), called by the snapshot job cma-snapshot-flash (every minute since 0009e, a date's take idempotent): a business date D is due at D + 1 at flash.snapshot_local_time in the tenant's zone and each run takes the latest due date unless a succeeded run holds it; a date that stops being the latest due one without a take is recorded as a missed run by the next take (since 0008zn)

tables.name: flash_snapshot
tables.what: The figures of every Flash overview per business date as the live computation gave them at the take: one row per grouping set, dims (codes: market, store, status, pipeline id) and measures (counts, ages, amounts per currency); no id of a record, no @ (0008zn). Insert only
tables.how: Written by the take only (cma.flash_snapshot_take, called by cma-snapshot-flash once per tenant and business date) through cma.flash_compute_of as of that date (the live computation, one code path); the application reads; never changed

tables.name: flash_snapshot_ids
tables.what: At each month end the frozen ids of the active customers, the active subscriptions and every device, with connection, market and state (0008zn). Insert only
tables.how: Written by the take only (cma.flash_snapshot_ids_write_of, in the take of a month's last business date; the application reads); removed after flash.id_list_retention_months (84) by the take (cma.flash_snapshot_ids_expire_of(tenant): its cutoff from the tenant's today, no caller's date), one audit row per removal; no row-level audit trigger

tables.name: flash_current_take
tables.what: The current take: per tenant and stock overview in flash.current_overviews (every stock overview but data quality by default since 0009p; the Flash landing's cards read their headline from it, cma.flash_cards_now) the figures of the overview's now, one row per grouping set (dims as codes, measures as numbers; no ids and no customer data), as cma.flash_compute_of gave them, with the definition version and when they were computed (computed_at, the page's Refreshed at). One take per tenant, overview and grouping set, replaced whole on refresh, so it does not grow (0009e)
tables.how: Written by the snapshot job cma-snapshot-flash every minute through cma.flash_current_refresh (SECURITY DEFINER; the application reads and holds no insert, update or delete) when a take is older than flash.current_refresh_minutes (5 by default, 1 to 1440); removed when a tenant setting is written, changed or reset, and when one of seven catalogs it reads changes a column the take reads (device status, device component kind, maintenance rule, connection pipeline, stage, task status, task type; 0009f); not audited (as data_quality_snapshot); the page reads the live computation when no take is fresh enough

tables.name: flash_watch_finding
tables.what: The deterministic watch's findings after each snapshot: jump, flow_zero, source_stale, snapshot_missing, dq_rise, with the overview, dims (market, check, source), the value, the one before and the threshold; open or resolved (0008zn)
tables.how: Written and resolved by the take only (cma.flash_watch_of, in a subtransaction of its own at the end of each take; the application reads); a finding moves once from open to resolved

tables.name: active_take
tables.what: One row per tenant: when its stored take of Customers → Active was last computed or found unchanged against its inputs' change markers (computed_at, the page's History as of), the digest of those markers it was computed under (inputs_key), the business date the take's ages and lengths are of, how long the refresh took, the active customers and holding subscriptions it found, the attribution's history start (intake.start_date plus attribution.window_days), which is the date of the page's attribution note and no longer bounds the attribution, and whether a settings change marked it stale (0009l, decision D13). The page reads its history from the take and says so when the take is stale, older than customers.history_notice_minutes or missing
tables.how: Written by the job cma-refresh-active-customers every minute through cma.active_refresh (the scheduler's system user, customers.refresh) when the tenant's take is older than customers.refresh_minutes (5 by default, 1 to 1440) or a change of a setting it depends on marked it stale (attribution.*, customers.*, crm.customer_segments, the three flash.*_statuses settings, intake.start_date, telephony.connected_min_seconds, calls.conversation_min_talk_seconds, reports.fx_eur_rates and flash.device_bands; the mark is set in the setting's own transaction and counted, so one set while a refresh runs is kept; the refresh never runs there); removed with its rows when the tenant's store or subscriptions are no longer set up; not audited (as data_quality_snapshot: computed values, the sources are audited where they are written). A due run first reads the inputs' change markers (per table a row count and a sum over its rows: the subscriptions, their events, the devices, the stores' customers with their link to a contact, the orders, the CRM's contacts, the stores, the device statuses and models, the markets, the connections' kind and account and the tenant's time zone; kept in inputs_key) and computes only when they, the business date or a setting changed, or when forced; otherwise the take is left as it is and only computed_at moves. The markers do not hold the CRM's deals, calls, emails and associations, nor the telephony behind the acquisition channel and the courtesy calls: those follow at the next change of a marker or at the next business date, at most a day. A fill that changes a take table's size much is followed by an analyze of that table (cma.active_take_analyze).

tables.name: active_base
tables.what: The base of Customers → Active as the refresh stored it: one row per subscription the tenant holds (not merged, not never-subscribed) with its status, whether it holds a device and pays, its amount turned into a month, its billing word, its devices in the field per model, its holding interval (created, ended), its store customer with Flash's figures of it (segment, holding subscriptions, devices, amount spent; the customer's devices figure, customer_devices, is Flash's and no read of the page uses it: the page sums the devices in the field per subscription instead), the contact's id as Flash's customer list shows it, and the customer's acquisition channel with First orders' level and the reason when Unknown. Ids, codes, amounts and times only (0009l)
tables.how: Written by the job cma-refresh-active-customers every minute through cma.active_refresh (the scheduler's system user, customers.refresh) when the tenant's take is older than customers.refresh_minutes (5 by default, 1 to 1440) or a change of a setting it depends on marked it stale (attribution.*, customers.*, crm.customer_segments, the three flash.*_statuses settings, intake.start_date, telephony.connected_min_seconds, calls.conversation_min_talk_seconds, reports.fx_eur_rates and flash.device_bands; the mark is set in the setting's own transaction and counted, so one set while a refresh runs is kept; the refresh never runs there). Row by row: a row that reads the same is neither written nor locked, a subscription no longer in the base is deleted; not audited

tables.name: active_customer
tables.what: One row per store customer of the base: its store, market, segment, acquisition channel with level and Unknown reason, Customer start and age in whole months as of the take, whether it is an Active customer, its holding subscriptions and its devices (Devices per active customer: the devices in the field on its holding subscriptions), its realised value (the store's amount spent) and its Monthly recurring amount in its largest currency with the others beside it: the customer list's columns, with an index per sort key for keyset paging. Ids, codes, amounts and times only (0009l)
tables.how: Written by the job cma-refresh-active-customers every minute through cma.active_refresh (the scheduler's system user, customers.refresh) when the tenant's take is older than customers.refresh_minutes (5 by default, 1 to 1440) or a change of a setting it depends on marked it stale (attribution.*, customers.*, crm.customer_segments, the three flash.*_statuses settings, intake.start_date, telephony.connected_min_seconds, calls.conversation_min_talk_seconds, reports.fx_eur_rates and flash.device_bands; the mark is set in the setting's own transaction and counted, so one set while a refresh runs is kept; the refresh never runs there). Row by row from the stored base, as active_base; not audited

tables.name: active_spell
tables.what: A store customer's active spells: each maximal stretch in which at least one of its subscriptions holds a device, by the reconstruction from the subscriptions' created and ended times (a current pause ends it, a past pause counts as holding), with its length in whole months as of the take and whether it ended; the Customer lifetime (Kaplan–Meier) and the customer cohorts are computed from them (0009l)
tables.how: Written by the job cma-refresh-active-customers every minute through cma.active_refresh (the scheduler's system user, customers.refresh) when the tenant's take is older than customers.refresh_minutes (5 by default, 1 to 1440) or a change of a setting it depends on marked it stale (attribution.*, customers.*, crm.customer_segments, the three flash.*_statuses settings, intake.start_date, telephony.connected_min_seconds, calls.conversation_min_talk_seconds, reports.fx_eur_rates and flash.device_bands; the mark is set in the setting's own transaction and counted, so one set while a refresh runs is kept; the refresh never runs there). Rewritten whole only when the part of the base it is computed from, the business date or a setting it reads changed; not audited

tables.name: active_month
tables.what: The month ends of Customers → Active: per calendar month (the tenant's zone), market, segment and acquisition channel the customers that started, ended and held (kind customers), the subscriptions (subscriptions), the Monthly recurring amount per currency (amount), for the two month ends a change line compares with the customers with a subscription in a currency (currency_customers), and Flash's churn count of the last 30 business dates (churned_30d). Counts and amounts only (0009l)
tables.how: Written by the job cma-refresh-active-customers every minute through cma.active_refresh (the scheduler's system user, customers.refresh) when the tenant's take is older than customers.refresh_minutes (5 by default, 1 to 1440) or a change of a setting it depends on marked it stale (attribution.*, customers.*, crm.customer_segments, the three flash.*_statuses settings, intake.start_date, telephony.connected_min_seconds, calls.conversation_min_talk_seconds, reports.fx_eur_rates and flash.device_bands; the mark is set in the setting's own transaction and counted, so one set while a refresh runs is kept; the refresh never runs there). Rewritten whole with active_spell; Flash's churn count (churned_30d) is written again at every refresh, where it reads differently; not audited. cma_read.active_customer_month reads it for the readers

tables.name: active_cohort
tables.what: The customer cohorts: per month and per quarter of the Customer start, market, segment, acquisition channel and age in months of customers.cohort_ages_months, the customers started, those still in an active spell at their own start plus the age, and whether the row is Mature at the age. Counts only (0009l)
tables.how: Written by the job cma-refresh-active-customers every minute through cma.active_refresh (the scheduler's system user, customers.refresh) when the tenant's take is older than customers.refresh_minutes (5 by default, 1 to 1440) or a change of a setting it depends on marked it stale (attribution.*, customers.*, crm.customer_segments, the three flash.*_statuses settings, intake.start_date, telephony.connected_min_seconds, calls.conversation_min_talk_seconds, reports.fx_eur_rates and flash.device_bands; the mark is set in the setting's own transaction and counted, so one set while a refresh runs is kept; the refresh never runs there). Rewritten whole with active_spell, so its rows are of the moment of that rewrite (at least once per business date); not audited. cma_read.customer_cohort reads it for the readers

tables.name: active_document
tables.what: The answers of Customers → Active's reads as the refresh computed them (0009l, decision D16: the table first, the live present after): above the fold (part top: the tiles as of the take, the churn count, the series of month ends, the filters' choices) and below it (part rest: inflow and outflow, the amounts, the markets, the two segments compared, survival, age, the mix, the customers by number of devices (device_customers); without the cohorts, which a read takes from active_cohort for the months it shows), without a filter (an empty market, segment and channel) and under each single market, segment or acquisition channel. A read under those filters is a key lookup; a combination of filters is computed from the take's rows. Counts, codes and amounts only
tables.how: Written by the job cma-refresh-active-customers every minute through cma.active_refresh (the scheduler's system user, customers.refresh) when the tenant's take is older than customers.refresh_minutes (5 by default, 1 to 1440) or a change of a setting it depends on marked it stale (attribution.*, customers.*, crm.customer_segments, the three flash.*_statuses settings, intake.start_date, telephony.connected_min_seconds, calls.conversation_min_talk_seconds, reports.fx_eur_rates and flash.device_bands; the mark is set in the setting's own transaction and counted, so one set while a refresh runs is kept; the refresh never runs there). Computed at every refresh from the rows just stored and as of that take; a document that reads the same is neither written nor locked; not audited

tables.name: ingest_event
tables.what: Every incoming event and its processing state
tables.how: Each webhook or sync event; sweep retries every minute

tables.name: sync_run
tables.what: Every job run with counts
tables.how: Each sweep, form poll, email poll, reviews poll (hourly, since 0008ze), reconcile and backfill; since 0008r the scheduler's forgotten-day close too, without a connection; since 0008s the follow-up refresh every minute per tenant, without a connection; since 0008zi each device snapshot load (job assets_import), run by a person, no schedule; since 0008zj the asset register poll (job assets_poll) every 5 minutes, each connection when due, and its full snapshot in the nightly reconcile; since 0008zl the subscriptions poll (job subscriptions_poll) every 5 minutes, each connection when due, and a store's full read of its subscriptions in the nightly reconcile

tables.name: sync_cursor
tables.what: Where each job resumes
tables.how: Each job run

tables.name: outbox_action
tables.what: Actions out to the CRM
tables.how: Worker by hand; unused since 13 October

tables.name: audit_log
tables.what: Who changed what and when
tables.how: Database trigger on every change

derived.name: speed_to_lead
derived.what: Per lead: first call, agent, time to first attempt in business hours, within target

derived.name: lead_to_order
derived.what: Per lead: the first order it led to and days to order

derived.name: lead_cohorts
derived.what: Per lead deal: its ISO week and month of creation, age, first attempt and first conversation, outcome and time lost, first store order and days to order, not called yet (lead cohorts)

derived.name: intake_per_day_v
derived.what: Per day and market: forms, deals, tickets, calls, new customers, orders, renewals

derived.name: crm_record_detail
derived.what: Amount, currency, channel, category and the reason's option value of deals and tickets

derived.name: workday_summary
derived.what: Per workday: working, productive, paid and billable seconds, and the day's sessions (addition 0008zs)

derived.name: time_interval
derived.what: Every status interval with its length

derived.name: roster_published_entry
derived.what: The published version of every roster entry

derived.name: open_lead
derived.what: Every open lead deal not called: owner, market, age in business days and its bucket, past the target, the last call (0008o)

derived.name: open_ticket
derived.what: Every open ticket of a counted pipeline against its SLA: business minutes open, the SLA in force, ok, at risk, breached or no business hours, minutes to breach (0008o)

derived.name: open_task
derived.what: Every open task: type, priority, status, owner, due time and whether it is overdue, due today or later, the deal or ticket by id (0008o)

derived.name: follow_up_summary
derived.what: Per tenant: counts of leads not called and past the target, tickets at risk, breached and without owner, tasks overdue, due today and with an owner nobody maps to (0008o)

derived.name: follow_up_by_owner
derived.what: Per person (by id) and one row for owners nobody maps to: open leads, past the target, open tickets, at risk or breached, tasks overdue and due today (0008o)

derived.name: connection_pipeline_sla
derived.what: Per pipeline: its own SLA in business minutes, or null for the tenant default (0008o)

derived.name: email_waiting
derived.what: Open conversations whose latest message is the customer's: inbox, mailbox, market, waiting since, business and elapsed time, the link to the conversation

derived.name: email_not_responding
derived.what: Open lead deals whose contact got an agent email at least email.no_response_days ago with no email, inbox message or phone conversation back since: deal, pipeline, market, owner, the last email

derived.name: first_orders
derived.what: Per won deal of an order pipeline: market, when, the linked shop order by id, kind (first, repeat, renewal, not first, no contact), currency and amount, the evidence found before it (lead deal, conversation, email, phone match, attempt, known contact), its level, call center or self-service, days from the first touch, the credited person by id (0008u)

derived.name: callbacks_kept
derived.what: Per callback task (a counted callback type) since the intake start: due date, ISO week, the owner's person by id, kept, not kept, pending, without a contact or a due time, the keeping call's time and its minutes from the due time (0008w)

derived.name: attempts_per_deal
derived.what: Per sales deal (a lead pipeline, never an order pipeline) since the intake start: market, pipeline, stage, the owner's person by id, created, closed, the contacts' first order after the creation (ordered_at) and why the window ended (closed, ordered or open), the outcome (won, lost, ordered, unknown, open), the attempts in the window (outbound Aircall calls on the deal or its contacts; every outbound HubSpot call when attempts.source is crm), those that were a conversation (from the linked Aircall call only: connected, at least calls.conversation_min_talk_seconds of talk and no tag meaning not reached or incorrect data) and the first that was, talk time in all and on conversations, the first and last attempt, the speed to lead in business seconds and called before the next noon, for open deals the business days since the last attempt with its bucket, the attempts without an outcome and the HubSpot calls logged without an Aircall call. From HubSpot deals, contacts and calls, Aircall calls with their link, and shop orders; computed on read, so as current as the mirror (0008y, for sales since 0008z, conversations since 0008zc)

derived.name: deal_funnel_rows
derived.what: Per sales deal (a lead pipeline, never an order pipeline) since the intake start and per stage with a stored time: the deal's ids, pipeline, current stage and its outcome, the outcome, the reason's option value, market, created and closed, and the stage with its entry and exit; a deal without any stage time as one row without a stage. From HubSpot deals and their stage history; computed on read, so as current as the mirror (0008zb)

derived.name: cancellation_rows
derived.what: Per record of the tenant's cancellation kind (reports.cancellation_kind, matched by its rules) since the intake start: the kind, ids, pipeline, stage, created, open or closed, closed, the reason's option value and the market (the record's, else its contact's country). Requests, never contracts; computed on read (0008zb)

derived.name: reviews_per_day
derived.what: Per tenant and business day: the counted reviews (published, of a counted review channel), the average rating, the distribution by whole star, the negative ones, the link levels (order, contact, none) and the previous day's count and average. From the review platform's reviews, by the day they were submitted in the tenant's zone; computed on read (0008ze)

derived.name: reviews_per_week
derived.what: The same per ISO week, with the previous week's count and average (0008ze)

derived.name: reviews_per_market
derived.what: Per market and ISO week: the counted reviews, average rating, star distribution, negative ones, link levels and the previous week's count and average; the market is the review channel's, unknown when it has none (0008ze)

derived.name: reviews_per_channel
derived.what: Per review channel and ISO week: its name, market, the counted reviews, average rating, star distribution, negative ones, link levels and the previous week's count and average (0008ze)

derived.name: review_market_state
derived.what: Per active market: whether it has a counted review channel and whether that channel holds published reviews (no channel, channel without reviews, has reviews), with the channels and the published reviews they hold (0008ze)

derived.name: maintenance_due
derived.what: Every due item of the tracked devices as of each tenant's date: component or end of life, due date with its basis (recorded, rule, unknown), action date and month, past due, the planned exchange it belongs to (0008zi)

derived.name: maintenance_per_month
derived.what: Per action month, market and model: due items, component items, devices at end of life, planned exchanges whose first action date falls in the month, past due (0008zi)

derived.name: subscription_payment_state
derived.what: Per subscription the latest full read still returns: its payment state from the two subscription tables only: failed, paused, canceled (canceled or expired), in_retry (active with a failed renewal of a cycle no renewal of that cycle or a later one follows; its cycle, first failure and highest attempt), paid (active otherwise); merged and never-subscribed left out; awaiting payment not built (0008zl)

derived.name: courtesy_order
derived.what: One row per courtesy order since each tenant's courtesy.start_date as of now: order, store, market, segment, business and due dates, has_contact (never which contact), attempts, conversation, last attempt, completion, outcome, the completing person and state (0009a). Computed when read by cma.courtesy_orders_of from cma.commerce_order, cma.commerce_customer, cma.commerce_store (Shopify's webhooks and read-back, the nightly reconcile, the backfill) and cma.telephony_call, cma.telephony_call_tag, cma.call_link, cma.crm_call, cma.crm_association (Aircall's and HubSpot's webhooks, the call link each minute by ingest-sweep)

derived.name: active_customer_month
derived.what: Per tenant, calendar month, market, customer segment and acquisition channel: the active customers and the holding subscriptions at the month's end as reconstructed from the subscriptions' created and ended times (the running month as of the take; a past pause counts as holding), and the customers' inflow and outflow of the month; counts only, no customer and no contact (0009l). A plain view of the stored take (cma.active_month), so it is as of the take's History as of, refreshed by the job cma-refresh-active-customers

derived.name: customer_cohort
derived.what: Per tenant, customer cohort (the first day of the month or quarter of the Customer start; grouping says which), market, customer segment, acquisition channel and age in months of customers.cohort_ages_months: the customers started, those still in an active spell at their own start plus the age, and whether every customer of the row is that old (mature); counts only, no customer and no contact (0009l). A plain view of the stored take (cma.active_cohort), as of the take's History as of
